records.name: Bodine Street Garden
records.summary: Neighbors who share a community garden on South 3rd Street in Queen Village. The garden has no open plots, so new people join a long waiting list.
records.what_you_do: Join the waiting list for a plot. The site says the wait is 4 to 6 years, and the garden has no plots available now.

first_step.how: Fill out the Waiting List Signup form on the Get Involved page, which asks for your name, email, and Philly neighborhood.
first_step.basis: The page says there are no plots available and the wait is 4 to 6 years, so a newcomer cannot get a plot for years.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe open days, work days, or a first visit. Joining means getting on the waiting list, and the page does not say how or when people are contacted.
first_visit_tips: Have your Philadelphia neighborhood name ready for the form.
Questions that are not about the waiting list can go to the garden's email address or phone line.

records.notes: Status set to dormant from the News archive: the newest dated item is from February 2011, and copyright years are not evidence. The waiting list page has no date, so this may understate a live garden. The garden's own contact footer gives 914 South Bodine Street, while the tier 1 location (939-941 S 3rd Street, from the Neighborhood Gardens Trust listing) is kept. A person should check the address before publishing. The site has no open days, dues, or access notes.

records.name: Bogucki Foundation
records.summary: A charity that runs its own youth education workshops, health outreach, and social welfare help, and invites volunteers and partners through a contact form. The site does not say when or where its programs meet.
records.what_you_do: Send a message through the Contact Us form to ask about volunteering or partnering. The site names several programs (youth education, health and wellness, social welfare, and a fishing outing with police called Cops and Bobbers) but gives no dates or sign-up steps for any of them.

cost.text: Medical flights for families are free. The site does not list costs for its workshops or other programs.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us form on boguckifoundation.com to ask which programs take volunteers and how to sign up.
first_step.basis: The site invites volunteers and partners and offers a newsletter sign-up, but it gives no program dates, places, or sign-up steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a volunteer shift, how long it lasts, or who usually takes part. Its programs include youth workshops, health outreach, and home repair supply help, but it does not list where or when they meet.
first_visit_tips: Ask through the contact form which programs meet in Philadelphia before you plan to come.
Ask what to bring or wear, and whether volunteers get any training.

records.notes: Not confirmed: whether this is a private foundation, and whether its programs run in Philadelphia. ProPublica has no Form 990 data for it, and its tax exemption was issued in April 2025. The IRS listing gives a Philadelphia mailing address only. Places named on the site outside the city include a medical flight program and a veterans program run with the Greater Wildwood Elks. The contact name is a business (Bogucki Enterprises LLC). Publish is kept from tier 1 because nothing found disproves it, but the owner should review this record before it goes live. The copyright 2026 footer is not counted as evidence.

records.name: Brewerytown Garden
records.summary: Neighbors who share the work of a community garden at Master Street and North 27th Street. Members tend plots and help with the season's work, and the garden also runs free family programs on Sundays in summer.
records.what_you_do: Gardeners share the season's work, about half a day a month per household. Plots are full for the 2026 season, and the wait list is open to residents of 19121 and nearby Fairmount. The garden also runs family programs on Sundays from June through September.

schedule.text: Free family programs on Sundays from June through September. Start times are not listed on the site.

cost.text: No garden dues are listed on the pages we read. The Sunday family programs are described as free. Members give about half a day of work a month.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday family program at the garden (June through September), and confirm the start time with the garden first, since the site does not list one.
first_step.basis: The Sunday family programs are described as free and for families, but the site gives no start times or sign-up steps. Plot membership has a wait list of more than 160 households.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Sunday programs are described as health and wellness activities for families, but the site does not describe the activities or list start times. Plot membership is a different path: the wait list is long, and the site does not describe what a first work day looks like.
first_visit_tips: The garden is at North 27th and Master Streets, and the site also lists a Master Street address.
Confirm the start time by phone or email before you go.
Plots are full for the 2026 season, so a first visit will not get you a plot this year.

records.notes: The Sundays page points to a schedule for September 2025, but that schedule is in an image and could not be read. The events page dates to 2023 headings; its concert entry has no date and was not used. An older What We Do page was seen only in search results (not read) and gives a different Sunday window, so it was not used. The join page says the garden is full for the 2026 season and the wait could last several seasons, which is why newcomer friendliness is rated on the Sunday programs instead. Status and last sign of life are carried from tier 1.

records.name: Bridesburg United Methodist Church
records.summary: A United Methodist church in Bridesburg that holds a weekly Sunday service and runs a Tuesday food pantry for families in the 19137 and 19134 ZIP codes. The church describes itself as small and friendly.
records.what_you_do: Visitors can join the 9:30 am Sunday worship service. The food pantry runs Tuesdays from 11 am to 2 pm, and families register by calling on a Tuesday morning.

schedule.text: Food pantry on Tuesdays, 11 am to 2 pm. Register by calling on Tuesday morning. Worship service on Sundays at 9:30 am.

first_step.how: Come to the 9:30 am Sunday service as a visitor. The church says visitors are welcome. For the food pantry, call 215-288-7505 on a Tuesday morning.
first_step.basis: The church says visitors are welcome at its weekly Sunday service, and the pantry page says everyone is welcome and gives a phone number and a set morning to register.
first_step.what_to_expect: The church describes itself as a small, friendly congregation with a weekly service at 9:30 on Sunday. The site does not say whether the service is in person or online, what happens during it, or where it meets. The food pantry runs Tuesdays from 11 am to 2 pm, and the site does not describe what a pantry visit is like.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-288-7505 to confirm whether the Sunday service meets in person and where.
For the pantry, call on a Tuesday morning and ask whether your ZIP code is served, since the page names 19137 and 19134 but also says everyone is welcome.
The site does not list parking, transit, or accessibility details, so ask when you call.

records.notes: The worship location, whether the service is in person or online, and music ministry details are not stated on the church site. A Music Ministry page is linked from the church site and was not read. The only address on file is the pantry address (2717 Kirkbride Street, #19), which is not confirmed as the worship location. The site's only year is in the copyright line, so no dated news was used.

records.name: Building Brighter Futures
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that supports children and young people up to age 21 who are in or entering foster care. Neighbors help by donating money or hygiene supplies for Care Kits, or by sponsoring a family or child for the holidays.
records.what_you_do: Donate money or hygiene supplies for Care Kits, sponsor a family or child for a holiday, or ask the office how to help at events.

locations.label: Philadelphia, PA (no street address on the site)

cost.text: No event cost listed. Donations and sponsorships are welcome.

first_step.how: Call 267-742-7325 or email Admin@BuildingBrighterFuture.org on a weekday between 9 am and 4 pm to ask how to help with Care Kits or events.
first_step.basis: The site lists donations, sponsorships, and office contact details, but it has no volunteer steps, sign-up process, or current event listings.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say what a helper does at an event, how long a shift lasts, or where to drop off Care Kit supplies. The events it lists so far were holiday gatherings from 5 to 7 pm in 2024, so the donation page is the clearest way to help right away.
first_visit_tips: Ask the office for the Care Kit drop-off address and days before you bring supplies, since the site does not list them.
Ask whether volunteers need a background check or training.
Office hours are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm, and phone messages are taken on holidays.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the site is a December 14, 2024 holiday event, so status stays probably_active (about 22 months old) and last sign of life is 2024-12. The site has no volunteer page or event calendar. The 2025 and 2026 years on the site are copyright notices only. The Instagram link was noted but not read.

records.name: By My Side Parenting
records.summary: A parenting group in Fishtown that runs open playgroups, so families with babies and young children can play, learn and meet other parents.
records.what_you_do: Bring your little one to the Monday baby group (for children 12 months and under, older siblings welcome) or the Wednesday or Friday morning playgroup (for children birth to five, older siblings welcome) to play and talk with other families. The playgroup asks for a suggested $5 donation.

schedule.text: Baby group on Mondays, 12 to 1 pm, for children 12 months and under. Morning playgroup on Wednesdays and Fridays, 10 to 11:30 am, for children birth to five.

locations.label: Playgroup space in the back building of Atonement Lutheran Church

cost.text: The playgroup page asks for a suggested $5 donation per session and says no one is turned away for lack of money. It does not list a separate price for the Monday baby group.

access.notes: The playgroup space is up a flight of stairs; the page does not mention an elevator or stroller access. Nearest SEPTA stop named on the directions page: the Berks Street El stop, a few blocks away. Buses 5 and 25 stop at Frankford and Montgomery.

first_step.how: Come to the Wednesday or Friday 10 am playgroup at 1542 E Montgomery Ave, using the alley entrance and then the stairs.
first_step.basis: The playgroups are open to all families on posted weekly times with no registration listed, and the page says to come as you are. It does not say newcomers are specifically welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Playgroup is loosely planned, with free play, circle time, and a snack, and adults can get coffee or tea. Parents, grandparents, and caregivers come along, and the sessions last about an hour and a half. Staff and other parents share parenting tips while the children play.
first_visit_tips: Bring a $5 donation if you can; it is suggested, not required.
Walk down the alley, go through the white doors, and climb the stairs to the playgroup space.
Street parking is usually available during the day.

records.notes: No dated news or events on the site. The copyright footer (2023) is not evidence. The calendar page is an embedded Google Calendar with no readable entries, so status stays probably_active with no sign-of-life date. The Monday baby group has no stated fee or registration. Atonement Lutheran Church hosts the space and is listed as a lead.

records.name: CAIR Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a civil rights group for Muslim communities. It helps people report discrimination, publishes know your rights guides, runs a youth leadership program, and shares voter registration information.
records.what_you_do: Join the email or text list, report discrimination through the reporting form, attend seminars and workshops, or give monthly. The know your rights guides are free downloads.

cost.text: The mailing list and know your rights guides are free, and monthly giving is optional. The site does not list costs for most events.

first_step.how: Sign up for the email or text list on the CAIR Philadelphia website (pa.cair.com/mailing-list/).
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up for the list on the site, and the events list shows many workshops and talks, but the site does not say how to register for each one.
first_step.what_to_expect: The events page lists many dated workshops, trainings, and community talks from 2020 to 2026, including know your rights sessions. The site does not list costs or registration steps for most of them, so the list signup is the clearest first step.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the newest dates before you plan a visit.
The office is at 1501 Cherry Street, but the site does not list office hours, so call or email first.
Contact by email at info@philadelphia.cair.com, by voicemail at 267-515-6710, or by text at 215-253-3608.

records.notes: The events page lists about 150 items. This record uses only items with clear dates, and the 2026 items are the newest evidence (a banquet on October 3, 2026 is listed under past events, and the homepage shows an October 6, 2026 press item). One listing dated December 16, 2026 sits under a 2025 heading and was not used. A CAIR-Pittsburgh banquet appears on the page; it is a different chapter and was not used. The youth leadership program is for ages 12 to 18; how an individual enrolls is not stated. Office hours and most event costs are not stated.
